chunks: Al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, chose four of everything: He chose from the angels Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, peace be upon them all; and He chose from the Prophets four for the sword: Abraham, David, Moses, and I; and He chose from the families four, saying: 'Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran above all people.' And He chose from the lands four, saying, the Exalted and Mighty: 'By the Fig and the Olive, And the Mount of Sinai, And this City of Security.' The Fig is Medina, the Olive is Jerusalem, Mount of Sinai is Kufa, and this City of Security is Mecca. And He chose from the women four: Mary, Asiya, Khadijah, and Fatimah. And He chose from the Hajj four: Thajj, Ajj, Ihram, and Tawaf. As for Thajj, it is the slaughter; and Ajj is the noise of the people with the Talbiyah. And He chose from the months four: Rajab, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. And He chose from the days four: Friday, the Day of Tarwiah, the Day of Arafah, and the Day of Slaughter.
ai.seo_question: What are the four chosen angels, prophets, cities, and days in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* illustrates the Shia concept of divine preference (*Ihtiyar*) by enumerating four chosen entities across cosmic and ritual categories, linking them to specific theological and historical significances. Notably, it interprets the Quranic oaths in Surah At-Tin as referring to Medina, Jerusalem, Kufa, and Mecca, thereby elevating Kufa’s status in Shia tradition, and identifies the Prophet alongside Ibrahim, Dawud, and Musa as the four prophets chosen for the sword.
